audit.summary: Login screen renders correctly with OTP sign-in flow, but plaintext preview credentials and a debug info panel are visible in the UI — acceptable in a QA build but must not reach production.

findings.title: Debug credential hints exposed in live UI
findings.details: The screen renders a visible info block listing test phone numbers and OTPs for all 11 role previews (Guard → Vendor). This text is surfaced as UI content, not just a code comment or internal doc.
findings.expected: Production builds should contain no plaintext credential hints; QA/staging builds may display them only behind a feature flag or in a collapsible developer panel.
findings.observed: All preview credentials (e.g. '9999999999 / 123456' for Guard through Supplier) are rendered as visible screen text at runtime.

findings.title: PHASE 1 label visible on screen
findings.details: The text 'PHASE 1' appears as a UI label, presumably indicating a phased rollout marker. If intentional branding it is fine; if a debug tag it should be removed before GA.
findings.expected: Phase labels should not appear in end-user-facing UI unless they are deliberate product copy.

findings.title: PRD coverage gap — login screen requirements not included in supplied chunk
findings.details: The supplied PRD chunk covers only Section 10 (Out-of-Scope features). No direct login/authentication acceptance criteria were provided for a line-by-line comparison. No out-of-scope feature appears to be incorrectly present on this screen.
findings.expected: Full audit requires Section covering authentication / OTP sign-in UX requirements.
findings.observed: Screen content does not conflict with any out-of-scope boundary listed in Section 10.
